annotation_description: Playing Boros Garrison on turn 1 with no other lands on the battlefield means it enters tapped and requires returning a land to hand — but MiMo Timmy has no other lands in play to return. This means they must return the Boros Garrison itself to their hand (or if the trigger is mandatory and they control no other land, they still must bounce something they control — which is the Garrison itself). This effectively wastes the entire turn, as they end up with no land on the battlefield. They should have played a basic land (Mountain or Plains) this turn, then played Boros Garrison on turn 2 bouncing that basic land, which would leave them with Boros Garrison producing RW on turn 2 instead of being set back a full turn.

Playing a basic Island on turn 1 when Memorial to Genius (enters tapped, produces {U}) should be played instead. With no 1-mana plays in hand, turn 1 is the free turn to deploy a tapped land. Memorial to Genius produces the same blue mana but entering it tapped later will cost tempo when curving into Rootha (turn 3) or Zaffai (turn 4).

Discarded Sunken Hollow (Island Swamp dual land) instead of basic Swamp. Sunken Hollow provides both U and B mana, and its Island type enables Nimbus Maze to produce W. Losing this dual land meaningfully weakens the mana base.

On turn 2, playing Island instead of Swiftwater Cliffs is suboptimal. Swiftwater Cliffs enters tapped, so playing it now (when you likely don't need the mana immediately on turn 2) means it will be untapped and ready on turn 3. Playing Island now wastes the opportunity to get the tapped land out of the way early. On turn 3, you'll want to play a land that enters untapped to cast Commander's Sphere (costs 3). If you play Island now, you'll need to play Swiftwater Cliffs on turn 3 (entering tapped), delaying Commander's Sphere to turn 4. Playing Swiftwater Cliffs now and Island on turn 3 gives you Mountain + Swiftwater Cliffs + Island = 3 mana on turn 3 for Commander's Sphere.

Playing a basic Mountain instead of Boros Garrison on turn 2 is suboptimal. Boros Garrison enters tapped but produces two mana (R+W) on subsequent turns, effectively ramping the player. Playing it on turn 2 (bouncing the existing Mountain) would mean having access to RW on turn 3 plus whatever other land is played. With expensive cards in hand like Combustible Gearhulk (6 mana) and Chain Reaction (4 mana), ramping via Boros Garrison early is important. Playing a basic Mountain instead delays the ramp by a turn.

On turn 2 with a hand full of expensive spells (Call the Skybreaker at 7 mana, Elemental Masterpiece at 7, Treasure Cruise at 8, Fiery Encore at 5), the player chose a basic Mountain over Memorial to Genius or Blighted Cataract. While Memorial to Genius enters tapped (costing tempo this turn), it provides a built-in card draw engine later in the game. Blighted Cataract also enters tapped but offers similar utility. Given that the hand is extremely top-heavy with no plays before turn 3 at the earliest (Rootha at 3 mana), playing a tapped land on turn 2 costs very little tempo since there's nothing to cast anyway. Memorial to Genius would provide blue mana (useful for the U-heavy spells) plus a valuable card draw sacrifice ability for the mid-to-late game.

Temple of the False God only produces mana if you control five or more lands. With only 2 lands in play (Mountain, Island), Temple will be a dead land for several turns. Swiftwater Cliffs enters tapped but immediately provides colored mana (U or R) on the next turn, which helps cast Commander's Sphere on turn 4 or Pramikon on curve. Playing Temple now means having 3 lands but only 2 that can produce mana, effectively wasting the land drop's tempo.

With 8 cards in hand and only 7 allowed, Kimi25 will be forced to discard at end of turn. They had exactly enough mana (Island + Mountain = {1}{R}) to use Fiery Fall's basic landcycling to fetch a basic land, converting a discard into land acceleration. Alternatively, they could have discarded Elemental Masterpiece for {U/R}{U/R} to create a Treasure token, turning a dead discard into mana ramp.

Discarding Blighted Cataract (a land) instead of a high-cost spell is suboptimal. Kimi25 has only 2 lands on the battlefield and is behind on mana development. Blighted Cataract is a land that could be played next turn to help catch up, and it also has a useful late-game sacrifice ability for card draw. Meanwhile, cards like Call the Skybreaker (7 mana) or Elemental Masterpiece (7 mana) are extremely expensive and won't be castable for many turns. Elemental Masterpiece can even be discarded later for value (its channel ability creates a Treasure token), and Call the Skybreaker has retrace so it's actually better in the graveyard. Discarding a playable land when mana-screwed at 2 lands is a meaningful error.

Playing Swiftwater Cliffs (enters tapped) instead of Island means the player cannot cast Commander's Sphere this turn. With Temple of the False God (which requires 5 lands to activate), getting to 4 untapped lands this turn by playing Island would allow casting Commander's Sphere (3 mana) to accelerate toward 5 lands and enable Temple next turn. Playing the tapped land delays mana development by a turn.

Kimi25 is severely mana-screwed (2 lands on turn 4) with 8 cards in hand about to discard to 7. They have Island + Mountain untapped and could use Elemental Masterpiece's discard ability ({U/R}{U/R}) to create a Treasure token, converting a card they'd otherwise discard into ramp. They're about to discard anyway, so this is pure upside - both reducing discard pain and creating much-needed mana acceleration.

Discarding Fiery Fall over Desert of the Fervent is suboptimal. Desert of the Fervent is a tapped land that only produces red mana - with only 2 lands in play (Island, Mountain) and Memorial to Genius in hand, Kimi25 desperately needs to hit land drops. However, Desert of the Fervent enters tapped and is strictly worse than a basic Mountain. More importantly, Fiery Fall has Basic Landcycling for {1}{R}, which means it can find any basic land and effectively acts as a land itself while also being a reasonable removal spell. Discarding it removes that flexibility. Meanwhile, several cards in hand like Call the Skybreaker and Elemental Masterpiece have retrace/discard synergies that specifically want land cards to discard - Desert of the Fervent would be perfect fuel for Call the Skybreaker's retrace or Elemental Masterpiece's treasure-making ability later. Keeping Fiery Fall (which finds lands) and Desert of the Fervent (which is discard fuel for retrace) would have been better than discarding the flexible Fiery Fall.

With 3 mana available (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet), casting Baleful Strix (UB, draws a card) is reasonable but Dungeon Map (3 generic) could also be cast. However, the main issue is that Propaganda (2U) is likely a stronger play here. In a 4-player game on turn 5 with no board presence and no blockers, Propaganda provides critical defensive value against attacks from multiple opponents. Baleful Strix is a fine blocker with deathtouch but only blocks one creature, while Propaganda taxes all attackers. The Strix's card draw is nice but Propaganda's persistent protection is more impactful at this stage. That said, Baleful Strix does draw a card and provide a deathtouch blocker, so this is debatable.

Propaganda was cast when no creatures exist on the battlefield, providing no immediate value. Dungeon Map would have provided mana acceleration, enabling full-cost Mulldrifter next turn (drawing 2 cards and keeping the 2/2 flyer) and getting closer to casting Sunblast Angel.

Casting Commander's Sphere before playing a land means Temple of the False God stays inactive (only 4 lands). Playing Plains first would give 5 lands, activating Temple for {C}{C}, providing significantly more mana this turn — potentially enough to cast both Commander's Sphere and Pramikon, Sky Rampart.

Playing Secluded Steppe (which enters tapped) instead of Boros Garrison wastes mana development. With 3 lands (Mountain, Plains, Mountain), playing Boros Garrison would bounce a Mountain, then next turn have access to RW + remaining lands. More importantly, the player could have played a normal land and cast Battlemage's Bracers (2R = 3 mana) this turn with their 3 untapped lands, developing the board. Instead, Secluded Steppe enters tapped and produces only W, leaving them with no spell cast this turn. The reasoning even cuts off mid-thought about wanting to cast Combustible Gearhulk, suggesting the player didn't fully evaluate the options. Playing Boros Garrison would have been better for mana development (adding RW production), or if they wanted to cast something this turn, they already had the mana for Battlemage's Bracers before playing any land.

MiMo Timmy had exactly 3 untapped mana and declined to cast either Thousand-Year Elixir or Battlemage's Bracers, both excellent setup pieces for their commander Osgir. Thousand-Year Elixir is particularly strong as it would let Osgir use his tap ability immediately upon entering, enabling the Meteor Golem reanimation from graveyard. The player appeared confused, thinking about Combustible Gearhulk instead of the actual options presented.

Kimi25 Libby has 8 cards in hand and needs to discard to 7. They could have discarded Elemental Masterpiece to create a Treasure token (its channel ability costs {U/R}{U/R} to discard and create a Treasure), which would provide mana acceleration. Instead, they passed on using the Elemental Masterpiece's discard ability and will just discard a card for no value during cleanup. However, looking more carefully, the Elemental Masterpiece discard ability costs {U/R}{U/R} and Kimi25 has no untapped lands (only Island and Mountain, both appear untapped actually). With Island and Mountain untapped, they could pay {U}{R} to activate Elemental Masterpiece's ability, discarding it to create a Treasure token. This would reduce their hand to 7 naturally while creating a Treasure, rather than losing a card for nothing in the discard step.

Discarding Desert of the Fervent over Mountain loses value. Desert of the Fervent can cycle for a card draw later, making it strictly better than a basic Mountain as a discard. Meanwhile, a basic Mountain has no additional utility beyond being a land. Both Call the Skybreaker and Oona's Grace (retrace cards) want land discards later, but any land works for that purpose - and Desert has cycling upside if drawn/played. The player should discard the basic Mountain instead, preserving the Desert's cycling option.

Evoking Mulldrifter draws 2 cards but leaves no board presence and uses all mana. Baleful Strix draws 1 card, leaves a 1/1 flying deathtouch blocker, costs less mana, and critically has excellent synergy with Phantom Steed in hand - which could repeatedly create copies to draw additional cards on attacks.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: GPT5m Gramps chose to cast Mulldrifter for its full cost {4}{U} instead of evoking it for {2}{U}. While keeping a 2/2 flyer is nice, the player only has 4 lands and an Arcane Signet (5 mana total), meaning casting Mulldrifter for full cost uses all their mana this turn. They have Baleful Strix (UB, 2 mana) and Dungeon Map (3 mana) in hand that could have been deployed alongside an evoked Mulldrifter. Additionally, the player has Phantom Steed in hand which could later blink creatures for value, but they also have Sefris as their commander who triggers on creatures going to the graveyard - evoking Mulldrifter would trigger Sefris's dungeon venture ability when it dies. However, since Sefris isn't on the battlefield yet, the graveyard synergy argument doesn't apply right now. The main consideration is tempo: paying full cost leaves no mana for other plays this turn, while evoking would allow deploying another card. With Phantom Steed in hand (which could copy the Mulldrifter if it stayed), keeping the body has some future value. This is debatable but spending all mana on a 2/2 flyer when you could have developed more board presence is slightly questionable.

Baleful Strix is a 2-mana card that draws a card on ETB and provides a 1/1 flying deathtouch blocker — excellent value. Dungeon Map is a 3-mana artifact that only taps for colorless and requires 3 more mana to venture into the dungeon. With Sefris as the likely commander (given the WUB color identity and dungeon synergy), Dungeon Map has some synergy, but the player has 4 mana available (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet, and Propaganda doesn't tap for mana). Actually, looking more carefully: Nimbus Maze + Swamp + Arcane Signet = 3 mana available. With 3 mana, they can cast either Dungeon Map (3) or Baleful Strix (UB = 2 mana, leaving 1 unused). Baleful Strix draws a card immediately, provides a relevant blocker with deathtouch and flying, and triggers Sefris's venture ability if it dies. Dungeon Map is a slow mana rock that won't provide meaningful value for several turns. Playing Baleful Strix would have been better — it replaces itself and provides board presence, while Dungeon Map is a tempo-negative play that doesn't impact the board.

Playing Island instead of Plains is suboptimal. With the current mana base (Mountain, Island, Temple of the False God, Swiftwater Cliffs, Commander's Sphere), the player already has access to blue mana from multiple sources but has no white source besides Commander's Sphere. Playing Plains would enable casting Pramikon, Sky Rampart (URW) or Gerrard, Weatherlight Hero (2RW) more reliably without needing Commander's Sphere for white. Additionally, playing Plains first and then potentially casting Pramikon (which requires U, R, and W) would be possible using Island + Swiftwater Cliffs/Mountain + Plains. Playing Island adds redundant blue mana while leaving the player vulnerable to not having white mana if Commander's Sphere is destroyed.

When casting Pramikon, Sky Rampart ({U}{R}{W}), the player chose Blue for what appears to be Commander's Sphere's mana production. Since Commander's Sphere is their only source of White mana, they should have chosen White from it and used their Islands for Blue and Mountain for Red. Choosing Blue from the Sphere means they may not be able to pay the W in Pramikon's cost.

Llama4 Valley has 6 lands (including Temple of the False God for 2 mana) and Commander's Sphere, giving access to significant mana. They chose to do nothing and pass the turn, wasting all their mana. Crackling Drake (UURR) could be cast with the available mana (2 Islands, Mountain, Swiftwater Cliffs, Temple of the False God for 2, Commander's Sphere) providing a flying threat that draws a card on entry. Gerrard, Weatherlight Hero (2RW) could also be cast using Commander's Sphere for white. Even Oona's Grace (2U) to draw a card would have been better than doing nothing. Passing with a full hand and unused mana is a significant waste of tempo in the mid-game.

Thousand-Year Elixir has excellent synergy with Feldon of the Third Path (also in hand), allowing Feldon to activate immediately on the turn he's played and potentially untap for a second activation copying Meteor Golem from the graveyard. Discarding it removes a key engine piece.

Kimi25 Libby has Elemental Masterpiece in hand, which can be discarded for {U/R}{U/R} to create a Treasure token. With only 2 lands in play (Island, Mountain) and a hand full of expensive spells (Call the Skybreaker at 7 mana, Treasure Cruise at 8, Fiery Encore at 5), ramping via a Treasure token would be valuable. This is an end-of-opponent's-turn opportunity to use mana that would otherwise go unused, creating a Treasure that helps cast future spells. The Elemental Masterpiece is extremely expensive at 7 mana and unlikely to be cast for full value anytime soon, so converting it to a Treasure is almost certainly correct.

With 5 mana available (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet, and potentially Dungeon Map for colorless), GPT5m Gramps could cast Mulldrifter (4U) to draw two cards, which provides the same card draw as Baleful Strix (one card) but draws an extra card. However, the real issue is sequencing: Baleful Strix costs only UB (2 mana), leaving 3 mana open, while Mulldrifter costs 4U (5 mana) and would use all available mana. Playing Baleful Strix now is reasonable for tempo since it leaves mana open for Dungeon Map activation or holding up interaction. But the player has Vanish into Memory and Swords to Plowshares as instant-speed interaction, and there are currently no threatening creatures on the board to respond to. Mulldrifter for 5 mana (drawing 2 cards) would have been slightly better value since there's nothing urgent to hold mana for, and the extra card draw helps find lands and threats. Alternatively, evoking Mulldrifter for 2U draws 2 cards for 3 mana, which is strictly better card advantage than Baleful Strix's 1 card for 2 mana, while still leaving 2 mana open.

Kimi25 Libby has 3 lands (Island, Mountain, Memorial to Genius tapped) and is holding Desert of the Mindful, which enters tapped. They have 7 cards in hand with expensive spells (Call the Skybreaker at 7 mana, Elemental Masterpiece at 7 mana, Treasure Cruise at 8 mana, Fiery Encore at 5 mana). Playing Desert of the Mindful as their land drop this turn would advance them toward casting these spells. Additionally, they could have used the Elemental Masterpiece's discard ability ({U/R}{U/R}, discard: create a Treasure token) to ramp, though that would cost 2 mana they may want to hold. The main issue is missing the land drop - they should play Desert of the Mindful before passing. The choice 'Desert of the Mindful' was available and they declined it.

Increasing Vengeance copies a target instant or sorcery spell YOU control. The only spell on the stack is Oona's Grace, which was cast by another player (likely Llama4 Valley themselves given it's their turn, but looking at context, it appears to be on the stack during their main phase). However, the key issue is that Increasing Vengeance costs RR and copying Oona's Grace (which draws a card) is a marginal use. More importantly, Commander's Sphere could be sacrificed to draw a card without spending mana from the pool, preserving the Increasing Vengeance for a much higher-impact spell later in the game (like copying a Chain Reaction, Call the Skybreaker, or other powerful sorcery). Increasing Vengeance also has flashback, but at 3RR - using it now to copy a simple cantrip wastes a powerful spell-copying effect that could be game-changing later.

With exactly URW available from untapped Mountain, Island, and Plains, Llama4 could cast Pramikon, Sky Rampart - a powerful defensive creature that restricts attack directions in multiplayer. Instead, they appear to have sacrificed Commander's Sphere to draw a card, losing both a mana source and the opportunity to deploy a key defensive piece.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: MiMo Timmy is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Chain Reaction and Combustible Gearhulk. With only 4 lands (and Boros Garrison in hand which would bounce one), the 6-mana Combustible Gearhulk is expensive but represents a powerful threat with first strike and card draw/damage. More importantly, discarding Combustible Gearhulk to the graveyard has strong synergy with Feldon of the Third Path (which is still in hand) - Feldon can reanimate a copy of Gearhulk for just 2R, getting its ETB trigger. Chain Reaction is a board wipe that currently has limited value since there are very few creatures on the battlefield. However, Boros Garrison is a tap-land that bounces a land and doesn't accelerate much in a deck that needs to get to 6 mana for Sun Titan. Discarding Boros Garrison instead of Combustible Gearhulk would have been better - the Gearhulk is a premium Feldon target and a strong card to cast naturally, while Boros Garrison is a mediocre land. Actually, keeping Combustible Gearhulk as a Feldon target makes the Gearhulk discard somewhat defensible since it goes to the graveyard where Feldon wants it. But discarding both Chain Reaction AND Combustible Gearhulk means losing a board wipe. The better line was to discard Boros Garrison (a tapped land that bounces another land, poor tempo) and either Chain Reaction or Battlemage's Bracers. Actually, re-reading: Combustible Gearhulk in the graveyard IS good with Feldon. And Chain Reaction has limited current utility. But Boros Garrison should have been a discard candidate over Chain Reaction since Chain Reaction is a board wipe that could be critical later, and Reconstruct History can get it back. The discard of Chain Reaction over Boros Garrison is the questionable part.

Playing Desert of the Mindful (enters tapped) instead of Mountain when both are in hand. While Rootha can still be cast either way, playing Mountain would leave an extra mana available this turn for potential flexibility.

With only 4 lands (one tapped) and 3 untapped lands producing at most 3 mana, Kimi25 can cast Rootha (1UR = 3 mana) but this is a 1/4 body that needs spells to copy and mana to activate (2 + bounce). Meanwhile, Elemental Masterpiece could be discarded for its hybrid cycling ability ({U/R}{U/R}, discard: create a Treasure token), which would ramp toward the powerful 7-mana spells in hand (Call the Skybreaker, Treasure Cruise). Rootha on turn 7 with only 4 lands and no immediate spell to copy is low-impact. However, this is a reasonable enough play since Rootha provides a body and future value, so the mistake is relatively minor.

Discarding Cloudblazer over Wand of Orcus at end of turn cleanup. Cloudblazer is a strong ETB creature (draw 2, gain 2 life) that synergizes well with Phantom Steed (which can repeatedly flicker it for value). Wand of Orcus requires black mana and an equipped creature to be relevant, and its Zombie-generating ability is less synergistic with this deck's gameplan. The deck appears to be a Sefris/Esper deck but the current board doesn't have strong equipment targets, making Wand of Orcus the weaker card to keep.

Kimi25 Libby chose to cast Traumatic Visions (a 5-mana counterspell) from hand, presumably to hold up as a counter. However, looking at the choices, 'Unknown (bdae9dce)' is likely Rootha's bounce ability or a land play option. More importantly, Treasure Cruise could be cast here using Delve - with 3 cards in the graveyard (Blighted Cataract, Fiery Fall, Desert of the Fervent), they could exile all 3 to cast Treasure Cruise for just 4U (5 mana total), which they have available (Island, Mountain, Memorial to Genius, Desert of the Mindful, Mountain = 5 lands plus Rootha). Drawing 3 cards for 5 mana is far better than holding up a 5-mana counterspell, especially when the hand is full of expensive spells and needs to develop. The player has 6 lands (including Rootha which isn't a land) - actually 5 lands. With 5 mana they could Delve away 3 cards and pay 4U for Treasure Cruise, drawing 3 fresh cards to find lands and cheaper interaction. Instead casting Traumatic Visions as a counterspell means tapping out anyway but getting no card advantage, and holding a clunky 5-mana counter is poor when you need to develop your board. Actually, re-reading - they may be casting it for its basic landcycling ({1}{U}) to search for a basic land, which would cost only 2 mana and fix/ramp. That's more reasonable but still worse than Treasure Cruise which draws 3 cards.

Rootha, Mercurial Artist (1/4) could have attacked MiMo Timmy or Llama4 Valley for free - neither has any blockers. Rootha's bounce ability can still be activated even while attacking, so there's essentially no risk. However, 1 damage in Commander is extremely marginal.

Attacking with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into a 4-player game where it's the only creature GPT5m Gramps controls. While it has flying and deathtouch making it a decent attacker, it's also a valuable blocker - deathtouch deters attacks, and Gramps has Propaganda but losing the Strix means losing a defensive piece. Additionally, Gramps has Phantom Steed in hand which could exile and repeatedly copy the Strix for value if it stays on the battlefield. Trading away the Strix for 1 damage is low value compared to keeping it as a blocker and Phantom Steed target.

Llama4 Valley had 8+ mana available (including Temple of the False God and Commander's Sphere) and multiple strong castable cards in hand including Pramikon, Sky Rampart (URW), Ral Zarek (2UR), River Kelpie (3UU), Guttersnipe (2R), Gerrard (2RW), and Wall of Stolen Identity (3U), but chose to only play an Island and pass the turn, completely wasting a turn's worth of mana development.

With only 4 lands on the battlefield and a hand full of expensive spells (Sun Titan at 6, Jor Kadeen at 5, Triplicate Titan at 9, Reconstruct History at 4), discarding the only land in hand risks missing critical land drops needed to deploy any of these threats.

GPT5m Gramps has Sunblast Angel in hand, which destroys all tapped creatures when it enters. By attacking with Baleful Strix, it becomes tapped. If Gramps plans to cast Sunblast Angel in a future turn (or even this turn in main phase 2), having their own Baleful Strix tapped would mean it gets destroyed by their own Sunblast Angel. Additionally, Baleful Strix is a 1/1 with deathtouch and flying - attacking into a board where Kimi25 Libby has Talrand (2/2) and Rootha available, and the attack direction matters in a Pramikon game. The Strix is more valuable as a blocker with deathtouch and Propaganda is already discouraging attacks. However, the 1 damage chip is very marginal and risks losing a deathtouch blocker that synergizes with Propaganda for defense. The real cost is minor since the Strix has already drawn its card, but attacking it into potential blocks or tapping it before a potential Sunblast Angel play is slightly suboptimal.

Kimi25 Libby had 2 untapped lands (Mountain + Memorial to Genius) and could have discarded Elemental Masterpiece for {U/R}{U/R} to create a Treasure token. This would convert an expensive 7-mana sorcery they're unlikely to cast soon into ramp, while also putting an instant/sorcery in the graveyard to buff the Inferno Project in hand. The mana was going unused anyway.

Discarded Mulldrifter, one of the best cards in hand, instead of a redundant basic land. GPT5m Gramps is severely mana-screwed (only 2 lands + Arcane Signet + Dungeon Map) and Mulldrifter could be evoked for just 2U to draw 2 cards to dig out of mana screw. It also has excellent synergy with Phantom Steed in hand (repeated ETB triggers drawing 2 cards per attack). Meanwhile they have 4 lands in hand including a redundant Swamp (already have one on battlefield plus Command Tower for black).

Llama4 Valley has 8 lands (including Temple of the False God for 2 mana and Commander's Sphere for 1) giving access to approximately 9 mana. Playing Guttersnipe (3 mana) is fine value, but Pramikon, Sky Rampart (3 mana URW) is a strong defensive option that controls combat in a 4-player game, and River Kelpie (5 mana) provides card draw whenever permanents enter from graveyards (synergizing with graveyard strategies). However, the bigger consideration is sequencing: playing Empowered Autogenerator (4 mana) this turn would start accumulating charge counters for future mana acceleration, which is important given Zetalpa (8 mana) sitting in hand. Playing Guttersnipe is only good if you plan to chain instants/sorceries, but with Increasing Vengeance and Oona's Grace in the graveyard and few instant/sorcery spells in hand, the immediate payoff is limited. Empowered Autogenerator + Guttersnipe could both be cast this turn (4+3 = 7 mana, and they have ~9 available), making the sequencing of which to cast first relevant but both castable. The real question is whether Guttersnipe alone is the best single play versus deploying Empowered Autogenerator first to start ramping toward Zetalpa.

Only attacking with Rootha (1/4) instead of both creatures when there are opponents with no blockers available. MiMo Timmy has no creatures and Llama4 Valley is fully tapped. Talrand as a 2/2 isn't a meaningful blocker, and there's free damage being left on the table.

Kimi25 Libby had 6 untapped lands and could have activated Memorial to Genius ({4}{U}, {T}, Sacrifice: Draw two cards) at instant speed during combat. This is significant card advantage that was declined for no clear benefit, as the mana would likely go unused.

Kimi25 Libby chose not to attack with Rootha (1/4) and Talrand (2/2) when there were viable targets. MiMo Timmy has no blockers and is at 40 life, and Llama4 Valley has no blockers either. GPT5m Gramps has Propaganda up which taxes attacks, but the other two players are open. While the damage is small (1-3 points), there's essentially no downside to attacking an undefended player — Rootha is a 1/4 that survives most combat and Talrand is a 2/2 that could chip in. The reasoning given ('lending fees remain usurious') references Propaganda but that only applies to attacking Gramps. Free damage should generally be taken in Commander, especially when it costs nothing.

Discarded Fiery Encore over Inferno Project. Inferno Project costs 7 mana and would enter as roughly a 1/1 or 2/2 given the very few instant/sorcery cards in graveyard (only Fiery Fall). Fiery Encore has better synergy with Talrand (triggers Drake token) and Rootha (can be copied), and actually does something meaningful when cast.

GPT5m Gramps attacked with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into a board where Kimi25 Libby has Rootha, Mercurial Artist and Talrand, Sky Summoner. Baleful Strix is a valuable defensive piece - its deathtouch makes it an excellent blocker that deters attacks, and it synergizes with Phantom Steed in hand (exile it, get repeated ETB draws). With Propaganda already providing attack deterrence, the Strix is more valuable as a blocker/combo piece than as a 1-damage attacker. However, the 1 flying damage is free if nobody blocks, and Pramikon isn't on the battlefield to restrict attack directions, so the risk depends on who can block. Kimi25 Libby doesn't appear to have flying blockers currently, so the Strix would likely get through for 1. The risk is minimal but the upside is also minimal - 1 damage in a 4-player game at 37+ life totals is nearly irrelevant, while losing the Strix to any flash creature or combat trick would be bad.

During combat (on their own turn), Llama4 Valley chose to sacrifice Commander's Sphere to draw a card. Commander's Sphere is a mana rock that provides colored mana, and sacrificing it permanently removes a mana source. With expensive cards in hand like Zetalpa (8 mana) and only 8 lands/mana sources, losing a mana rock is significant. Additionally, this is their own combat step - they could use Oona's Grace (an instant) to draw a card by discarding a land, which is generally available from the graveyard via retrace anyway. More importantly, they could simply pass here and use Commander's Sphere for mana on future turns to cast their expensive spells, or at minimum wait until end of an opponent's turn to sacrifice it if they really want the card draw.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: Llama4 Valley cast Increasing Vengeance via Flashback (costing {3}{R}{R}) to copy Oona's Grace, which is an opponent's spell (Kimi25 Libby likely cast it). Increasing Vengeance can only target an instant or sorcery spell *you control*. Since Oona's Grace is not Llama4's spell, this is an illegal target, wasting the Flashback cast and exiling Increasing Vengeance for nothing. Even if the targeting were somehow valid, spending 5 mana and exiling a powerful spell from the graveyard just to copy a 'draw one card' spell is extremely poor value. The Commander's Sphere sacrifice (draw a card) or simply passing would have been far better uses of resources.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 4, min 4)
annotation_description: Discarding Phantom Steed (a 4-mana flash creature that synergizes well with Baleful Strix for repeated deathtouch blocking and card draw) instead of excess lands. GPT5m Gramps already has 4 lands + 2 mana rocks on the battlefield, so additional basic lands like Swamp or Island provide diminishing returns compared to a useful creature.

Cast Pramikon before playing the Mountain from hand. With the extra land played first, they would have had 9 mana available (including Temple of the False God), allowing them to cast Pramikon (3 mana) plus another significant spell like Ral Zarek (4 mana) or Burnished Hart (3 mana) in the same turn.
MiMo Timmy has no creatures on the battlefield, so Guttersnipe could attack for 2 free damage with zero risk. The confused reasoning suggests the player likely passed without attacking.

GPT5m Gramps has Propaganda on the battlefield, requiring {2} per attacking creature. Llama4 Valley has all lands tapped, so they cannot pay the Propaganda tax and Guttersnipe likely cannot legally attack GPT5m Gramps. MiMo Timmy has no blockers and no defensive enchantments, making them a free target for 2 damage.

Feldon of the Third Path with Triplicate Titan in the graveyard is an extremely threatening engine that can generate 9/9 tokens each turn. Playing a slow ramp artifact that enters tapped instead of addressing this threat is suboptimal.

Attacking with all creatures including Burnished Hart and Guttersnipe is suboptimal. Burnished Hart's sacrifice ability (search for 2 basic lands) is extremely valuable for ramping toward Zetalpa, Primal Dawn (8 mana) in hand. Guttersnipe is a key damage engine that should be preserved. Opponents have blockers (Baleful Strix with deathtouch, Rootha 1/4, Feldon 2/3) that can trade favorably.

Llama4 Valley appears to have passed combat without attacking. River Kelpie (3/3 with persist) could attack safely into MiMo Timmy who only has Feldon (2/3) as a blocker - if blocked, River Kelpie returns via persist and triggers a card draw. Burnished Hart could also contribute chip damage. Free or near-free attacks were missed.

MiMo Timmy cast Battlemage's Bracers (2R) before considering whether to use Feldon's ability this turn. With 5 lands (4 Mountains + 1 Plains + 1 Secluded Steppe), casting Bracers costs 3 mana, leaving only 2 mana available. Feldon's ability costs 2R+tap, so Timmy can't both cast Bracers AND activate Feldon this turn. Furthermore, equipping Bracers costs another 2 mana, so even next turn it would require 5 mana just to equip and activate Feldon. Hedron Archive (4 generic) would have been a strong alternative - it provides ramp to enable Feldon activations on future turns more reliably, and can be sacrificed for card draw later. Alternatively, casting Thopter Engineer (2R) would create an artifact creature token and give artifact creatures haste, providing board presence. The Bracers are only valuable once equipped to Feldon and activated, which requires significant additional mana investment. However, Bracers + Feldon is a powerful combo that doubles his reanimation value, so planning ahead for it is defensible.

Kimi25 Libby has Rootha (1/4) and Talrand (2/2) available to attack. Propaganda only affects attacks against GPT5m Gramps, so attacking other players is free. MiMo Timmy has Feldon (2/3) untapped but all lands tapped, and Llama4 Valley has Guttersnipe (2/2) with all lands tapped. Talrand could attack into Llama4 Valley (Guttersnipe can trade but Valley might not want to lose it) or MiMo Timmy. While the creatures are valuable, passing up free chip damage in a multiplayer game with no real downside is slightly suboptimal. Rootha is more defensible to hold back (1 power, useful ability), but Talrand could have gotten in for 2 damage somewhere relatively safely.

Discarded Sunbird's Invocation, one of the most powerful cards available in a hand full of high-MV spells. With Talrand on board and multiple 5-7 MV spells in hand, Sunbird's Invocation would generate massive cascading value once resolved.

Attacking with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) for 1 chip damage in a 4-player game where the defensive value of a flying deathtouch blocker is significant. While Propaganda provides some protection, losing the blocker for a full turn cycle (3 opponents' turns) for just 1 damage is likely not worth it.

Rolling Temblor kills Llama4's own Guttersnipe (a key synergy piece for their instant/sorcery strategy) while failing to kill the most dangerous creature on the board - Feldon of the Third Path (2/3 survives at 2/1) equipped with Battlemage's Bracers, which threatens to copy Triplicate Titan or Combustible Gearhulk from MiMo's graveyard. Additionally, the land (Izzet Guildgate) should be played before casting spells.

With River Kelpie on the battlefield, casting Faithless Looting from graveyard (flashback) first would trigger River Kelpie's 'whenever a player casts a spell from a graveyard, draw a card' ability, netting an extra card draw. Seeing those extra cards before committing to Ral Zarek would provide better information for the turn's decisions. Both spells are castable this turn (Looting flashback {2}{R} + Ral {2}{U}{R} = 7 mana, and Valley has 8 mana available).

MiMo Timmy cast Reconstruct History for 4 mana to recover 2 cards to hand, when they could have used Feldon of the Third Path's ability (2R, tap) to create a copy of Triplicate Titan (9/9 flying, vigilance, trample with haste) from the graveyard, providing massive immediate board presence. The Titan token would threaten significant damage this combat. With remaining 2 mana, Mind Stone could have been cast for future ramp.

message: Select up to one artifact card
annotation_description: MiMo Timmy chose Thousand-Year Elixir as the artifact to return with Reconstruct History, but Triplicate Titan is a far superior choice. Triplicate Titan is a 9/9 with flying, vigilance, and trample that creates three 3/3 tokens when it dies. More importantly, MiMo has Feldon of the Third Path on the battlefield, which can already create temporary copies of creatures in the graveyard - so keeping Triplicate Titan in the graveyard for Feldon isn't necessarily better than having it in hand. Thousand-Year Elixir costs 3 mana and gives haste to activated abilities and can untap creatures - it has synergy with Feldon but is much lower impact than a 9/9 threat. Combustible Gearhulk would also be a strong choice as a 6/6 first striker with card draw/damage ETB. The reasoning in the decision even acknowledges Triplicate Titan is huge but then pivots away without good justification.

Ral Zarek is a planeswalker controlled by an opponent (likely Llama4 Valley based on context) that can generate significant value with its +1 tap/untap ability and threatens an ultimate. MiMo Timmy chose to attack Kimi25 Libby (a player) instead of attacking Ral Zarek to remove it from the board. Removing planeswalkers that generate recurring value is generally higher priority than chipping away at a player's life total, especially when the attacker (Feldon) is only dealing 2 damage to a player at 36 life.
Kimi25 chose not to block what appears to be an incoming attack when Rootha, Mercurial Artist (1/4) could likely block a 3/3 River Kelpie without dying, preventing 3 damage for free.

Rootha, Mercurial Artist (1/4) could have blocked Feldon of the Third Path (2/3) with both creatures surviving the combat. This would have prevented 2 damage for free with no downside. Feldon is also a high-priority creature to trade with given its ability to reanimate Triplicate Titan and other powerful creatures from MiMo's graveyard.

Call the Skybreaker has Retrace, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard by discarding a land card. Discarding it to hand size actually makes it MORE accessible since it can be reused from the graveyard. However, Sol Ring costs only {1} and produces 2 mana - it's one of the most powerful cards in Commander and should have been played long ago (it only costs 1 mana). The real issue is that Sol Ring is still in hand on turn 15, and rather than discarding a less impactful card, the player chose Call the Skybreaker. While Call the Skybreaker with Retrace is fine to discard, the bigger problem is that Sol Ring should have been cast this turn or earlier. Looking at the board, Kimi25 Libby has 6 lands and Rootha + Talrand untapped - they had mana available to cast Sol Ring ({1}) at some point. Additionally, discarding Elemental Masterpiece would have been better since it has a discard ability that creates a Treasure token ({U/R}{U/R}, discard: create Treasure), but that requires paying mana. Actually, Call the Skybreaker with Retrace from graveyard is arguably better positioned there than in hand, so this discard isn't terrible. The real blunder is having Sol Ring in hand on turn 15 - but since the decision point is specifically about the discard, and Call the Skybreaker is actually a reasonable discard due to Retrace, the main issue is not discarding something less useful. Traumatic Visions or Talisman of Creativity could have been discarded instead, but Sol Ring at 1 mana should have been cast, and keeping it in hand to cast next turn is correct. Call the Skybreaker with Retrace from graveyard is actually a fine discard choice.

GPT5m Gramps skipped attacking entirely when they could have attacked Ral Zarek with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch). Attacking a planeswalker with an evasive creature is free value - removing loyalty counters from Ral Zarek is much more impactful than the 1/1 body sitting back on defense.

Cast Zetalpa despite potentially only having one white source (Plains). Additionally, casting Faithless Looting from graveyard would have triggered River Kelpie's draw ability (spell cast from graveyard) and could have been combined with Ral Zarek for significant value generation while still developing the board.

Zetalpa, Primal Dawn (mana value 8) is on the stack. Llama4 Valley has Refuse // Cooperate in hand, where Refuse deals damage equal to a spell's mana value to its controller. Casting Refuse would deal 8 damage to whoever cast Zetalpa, which is very significant. Instead, Valley passed priority and let the spell resolve without extracting this value.

Ral Zarek's +1 untaps a target permanent - Llama4 Valley chose to untap Zetalpa, Primal Dawn, which appears to be an opponent's extremely powerful creature (4/8 flying, double strike, vigilance, trample, indestructible). This gives the opponent's best threat full access to block and attack, rather than untapping one of Llama4 Valley's own tapped lands for mana advantage.

Attacking GPT5m Gramps with River Kelpie means paying {2} for Propaganda and risks the Kelpie being blocked and killed by Baleful Strix (deathtouch). MiMo Timmy at the same life total (28hp) has no blockers available and no attack tax.

Refuse targets a spell on the stack and deals damage equal to its mana value to that spell's controller. There is no opponent's spell on the stack during Llama4 Valley's own postcombat main phase. This wastes a card that has significant value as a reactive tool - Refuse can deal large damage when opponents cast expensive spells, and Cooperate can copy powerful spells.

Ral Zarek is a planeswalker on the battlefield that threatens extra turns with its ultimate and provides repeated value. Attacking a player at 34 life for 2 damage in Commander is nearly meaningless, while attacking Ral Zarek could remove or significantly weaken a dangerous permanent.

Thousand-Year Elixir has strong synergy with Feldon of the Third Path already on the battlefield - it can untap Feldon for a second activation each turn, and combined with Battlemage's Bracers, this enables copying powerful creatures like Triplicate Titan or Combustible Gearhulk from the graveyard multiple times. Study Hall is a mediocre colorless land that's less impactful.

Prismatic Strands is a defensive combat trick that prevents all damage from sources of a chosen color for the turn. Casting it during your own precombat main phase, when no opponent is attacking you and there's no damage to prevent, accomplishes absolutely nothing. The card is wasted for zero value. It has flashback (tap an untapped white creature you control), but the initial cast from hand is completely thrown away here. Deep Analysis from the graveyard (flashback for {1}{U} and 3 life) would have drawn 2 cards, and River Kelpie would have triggered (drawing another card when casting from graveyard), giving massive card advantage. Rolling Temblor from graveyard (flashback {4}{R}{R}) could also have been cast with River Kelpie synergy. Even Ral Zarek would have been a reasonable play adding a planeswalker to the board.

With only 1 card in hand and River Kelpie on the battlefield, passing without casting Deep Analysis from the graveyard via flashback ({1}{U}, pay 3 life) is a significant missed opportunity. River Kelpie triggers on spells cast from graveyard, so this would draw 3 total cards (2 from Deep Analysis + 1 from River Kelpie) at a very affordable cost of {1}{U} and 3 life when at 39 life.

Attacking GPT5m Gramps who has Propaganda (costing {2} to attack) and Baleful Strix (1/1 deathtouch that can trade with River Kelpie), when MiMo Timmy at 28hp has no available blockers and no tax effects.

MiMo Timmy has 6 lands (4 Mountains, 1 Plains, 1 Secluded Steppe) plus Feldon of the Third Path on the battlefield. With Feldon, they can already create token copies of creatures in the graveyard (like Triplicate Titan, Combustible Gearhulk, or Meteor Golem). The key issue is that Mind Stone is a 2-mana rock when they already have 6 lands and could instead be casting Sun Titan (4WW = 6 mana). Sun Titan is a 6/6 vigilance that returns permanents with MV 3 or less from graveyard to battlefield - it could bring back Thousand-Year Elixir (which synergizes amazingly with Feldon by letting him activate twice), Boros Garrison (ramp), or other key pieces. MiMo's mana is 4 Mountains + 1 Plains + 1 Secluded Steppe = they can produce 4R + 1W + 1W = 4RWW. Sun Titan costs 4WW, which is exactly castable with this mana. Playing Mind Stone instead means Sun Titan gets delayed a turn while providing minimal benefit since they already have enough mana for their key plays.

Kimi25 Libby has Rootha (1/4) and Talrand (2/2) on the board. GPT5m Gramps has Propaganda up requiring {2} per attacker, making attacking there expensive. However, Llama4 Valley at 39hp and MiMo Timmy at 28hp are open targets depending on attack direction (Pramikon is not on the battlefield). With no blockers that threaten to kill either creature favorably, attacking with at least Rootha (1 power, 4 toughness - very hard to lose in combat) into an opponent without Propaganda would be free chip damage. Declining to attack when you have safe attacks available leaves damage on the table.

Kimi25 Libby played a Mountain from hand instead of casting Sol Ring, which costs only 1 mana and would provide 2 colorless mana immediately. Sol Ring is one of the most efficient mana accelerants in Commander and should almost always be cast as early as possible. With 6 lands already on the battlefield (plus the Mountain about to be played making 7), they have plenty of colored sources. Playing the land is fine, but Sol Ring should have been cast as well - they had the mana to do both. Looking at the choices, Sol Ring costs {1} and they have untapped lands available. They could play Mountain AND cast Sol Ring, plus potentially cast Talisman of Creativity or even Treasure Cruise (with delve fuel from 8 cards in graveyard). By just playing Mountain and passing, they wasted significant mana and tempo.

Llama4 Valley has Deep Analysis in the graveyard and can flash it back for {1}{U} + 3 life (they have 39 life and only 1 card in hand). With 7 lands available (including Temple of the False God for 2 mana), they have plenty of mana. Drawing 2 cards when holding only 1 card would be very valuable. They also have Rolling Temblor flashback available for {4}{R}{R} and Oona's Grace retrace in the graveyard. Instead of using any of these options to rebuild their hand, they chose to pass to combat with essentially no board pressure (just River Kelpie) and only 1 card in hand.

Zetalpa, Primal Dawn has vigilance and indestructible, meaning there is zero downside to attacking with it every turn. It deals 8 damage per attack (4 power with double strike) and has flying so most creatures can't block it. Only attacking with 1 creature instead of both (especially Zetalpa) wastes significant damage output.

MiMo Timmy declined to activate Feldon of the Third Path during combat when being attacked by Zetalpa (4/8 flying, double strike, indestructible) for 8 damage. Feldon could create a Triplicate Titan token (9/9 flying) to block Zetalpa, absorbing all the damage. The titan token would survive combat (taking 8 total from double strike), then when sacrificed at end step, create three 3/3 golem tokens. This saves 8 damage and generates three tokens.

Llama4 Valley passed with Deep Analysis in their graveyard and River Kelpie on the battlefield. Flashing back Deep Analysis for {1}{U} and 3 life would draw 2 cards from the spell plus 1 card from River Kelpie's trigger (cast from graveyard), netting 3 cards when they only have 1 card in hand at 39 life. This is an extremely efficient play that was completely free in terms of board mana.

Kimi25 Libby used Traumatic Visions' basic landcycling ability during their own end step, which is a waste of a counterspell. Traumatic Visions is a 5-mana counterspell that can also be cycled for a basic land. With 8 cards in hand (including Traumatic Visions), they needed to discard to hand size anyway at end of turn. However, landcycling costs {1}{U} which uses mana, and more importantly, they threw away a counterspell when they could have simply discarded a less valuable card to hand size instead. With Elemental Masterpiece in hand (which can be discarded to create a Treasure token for {U/R}{U/R}), they had a card that could be productively discarded. The Traumatic Visions could have been kept as interaction to counter threatening spells from opponents. Additionally, they already have 8 lands on the battlefield (6 lands + Rootha + Talrand visible), so another basic land is less critical than keeping countermagic available.

GPT5m Gramps is attacking with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) while holding Sunblast Angel in hand. Sunblast Angel destroys all tapped creatures when it enters. By attacking with Baleful Strix, it will be tapped, and if Gramps later casts Sunblast Angel (which costs 4WW - they have Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet, and Dungeon Map for mana but likely need more lands), the Strix would be destroyed by their own Sunblast Angel. More importantly, the attack is into a board where the damage is minimal (1 damage) and Baleful Strix is much more valuable as a blocker with deathtouch, especially with Propaganda already providing defensive coverage. The risk of losing the Strix to blocks or removing it as a blocker far outweighs 1 point of damage. Additionally, with Sunblast Angel in hand, keeping creatures untapped is strategically important for when that angel is cast - you want opponents' creatures tapped, not your own.

Llama4 Valley has Deep Analysis in their graveyard and can flash it back for {1}{U} paying 3 life. With 7 lands on the battlefield (including Temple of the False God and multiple Islands), they have plenty of mana to cast it. Drawing two cards when they only have 1 card in hand (Farm // Market) would be significant card advantage. They also have Oona's Grace in the graveyard which could be cast via Retrace by discarding a land. River Kelpie is on the battlefield, which draws a card whenever a player casts a spell from a graveyard - so flashing back Deep Analysis would also trigger River Kelpie for an additional card draw (3 cards total for 3 life and {1}{U}). Additionally, Rolling Temblor flashback and Prismatic Strands flashback were available options. Passing with all that mana and graveyard value available while having only 1 card in hand is a significant missed opportunity.

MiMo Timmy has Feldon of the Third Path on board with Battlemage's Bracers and Triplicate Titan in the graveyard. By playing Darksteel Citadel and using 6 mana (2 to equip Bracers to Feldon, 3 to activate Feldon targeting Triplicate Titan, 1 to copy the ability via Bracers), they could create TWO 9/9 tokens with flying/vigilance/trample. Instead, casting Thopter Engineer for 3 mana first leaves insufficient mana for the equip+activate+copy line.

Attacking with Feldon of the Third Path risks losing MiMo Timmy's most important engine piece to blocks (Rootha 1/4, Talrand 2/2, River Kelpie 3/3 are all potential blockers). Feldon enables reanimating Triplicate Titan, Combustible Gearhulk, and Meteor Golem from the graveyard, which is far more valuable than 2 combat damage. Feldon also needs to stay untapped to use his activated ability.

Chose to attack Kimi25 Libby (31 life) instead of Ral Zarek, then skipped the attack entirely. Attacking Ral Zarek with the 1/1 flying deathtouch Baleful Strix would chip loyalty off a dangerous planeswalker, which is far more impactful than 1 damage to a player at 31 life. Even just selecting the wrong direction and then not attacking is a missed opportunity.

Llama4 Valley only attacked MiMo Timmy with 1 creature when MiMo Timmy had no creatures to block. With Zetalpa (4/8 double strike = 8 damage, plus has vigilance so no downside) and River Kelpie (3/3), attacking with both would deal 11 damage to the 20-life opponent instead of just 3 or 8.

Llama4 Valley declined to cast Prismatic Strands (from graveyard via flashback or from hand) to prevent damage from Zetalpa, Primal Dawn's attack. Zetalpa has double strike and deals significant damage. Choosing white with Prismatic Strands would have prevented all damage from the white Zetalpa this turn, saving 4+ life points.

Llama4 Valley passed the turn with only 1 card in hand while Deep Analysis was available to flashback from the graveyard for {1}{U} and 3 life. With River Kelpie on the battlefield, casting a spell from the graveyard would trigger an additional card draw, netting 3 cards total. At 39 life, the 3 life cost is negligible. They also had Ral Zarek available to cast.

GPT5m Gramps selected Kimi25 Libby as the attack target but then skipped the attack entirely. With a 1/1 flying deathtouch Baleful Strix, there's virtually no risk in attacking - it flies over ground creatures and deathtouch deters blocks. Additionally, if Ral Zarek is on the battlefield, attacking the planeswalker to reduce its loyalty would have been more impactful than even 1 chip damage to a player.

With 7+ lands and only 1 card in hand (nearly empty), casting a 3-mana rock provides marginal value. Deep Analysis is available via flashback from the graveyard for just {1}{U} + 3 life, drawing 2 cards. At 39 life, the 3 life cost is trivial. Both could be cast in the same turn (2 + 3 = 5 mana out of ~8 available), so at minimum Deep Analysis should have been cast first to see new cards before committing remaining mana.

MiMo Timmy is at 12 life with no creatures to block. Attacking with both Zetalpa (8 damage via double strike) and River Kelpie (3 damage) would deal 11 total, putting MiMo to 1. Instead, only 1 creature attacked, leaving MiMo at a much healthier life total. Against a player at 12 life, every point of damage matters.

Llama4 Valley passed the turn with only 1 card in hand while having Deep Analysis in the graveyard available for flashback ({1}{U}, pay 3 life). With River Kelpie on the battlefield, casting Deep Analysis from the graveyard would draw 2 cards (Deep Analysis) + 1 card (River Kelpie trigger for casting from graveyard) = 3 cards total, at a trivial 3 life cost from 39 life. Additionally, Ral Zarek could have been cast. Missing this free card advantage with a nearly empty hand is a significant error.

message: Select a permanent card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard
annotation_description: MiMo Timmy is at 5 life and chose to return a basic Mountain with Sun Titan's ETB trigger instead of Feldon of the Third Path, which is a powerful creature that could reanimate threats like Triplicate Titan or Combustible Gearhulk from the graveyard. With Battlemage's Bracers already on the battlefield, Feldon becomes even more powerful as its activated ability can be copied. A basic Mountain provides minimal value since MiMo already has lands and could play one from hand, while Feldon provides a recurring engine to generate threats and potentially stabilize at 5 life.

MiMo Timmy is at 5 life and chose to attack Kimi25 Libby (31 life) instead of Ral Zarek, a planeswalker that can deal 3 damage with its -2 ability. At 5 life, Ral Zarek's 3 damage represents a serious threat to MiMo's survival. Attacking a player at 31 life with presumably a single creature accomplishes very little.

MiMo Timmy is at 5 life with no untapped permanents and no creatures to block. Attacking with Rootha (1/4) would deal 1 free damage, bringing them to 4 life. Against a player this low, every point of chip damage matters and there is zero risk since MiMo has no blockers and all lands are tapped.

Forbidden Alchemy has flashback, meaning it can be cast from the graveyard for {6}{B}. Discarding it loses essentially nothing since it retains full functionality from the graveyard. Any other discard permanently loses access to that card.

MiMo Timmy is at 5 life with no creatures on the battlefield. Zetalpa alone deals 8 damage (lethal with double strike), and River Kelpie deals 3. Attacking with all available creatures guarantees the kill and leaves no room for tricks or errors. Choosing to attack with only 1 creature when 'All attack' was available is suboptimal - there's no downside to sending everything when the opponent has no blockers and you want to close out a player at 5 life.

When resolving Izzet Boilerworks' ETB trigger to bounce a land, chose to bounce a basic Island instead of Swiftwater Cliffs or Tranquil Cove, missing the opportunity to replay the bounce land later for a free 1 life gain from its ETB trigger.

Attacking with Baleful Strix into a board where Llama4 Valley has River Kelpie (3/3) that could block and kill the 1/1 Strix. While Strix has deathtouch and flying so it can only be blocked by flyers, and River Kelpie doesn't have flying, the real issue is that Baleful Strix is GPT5m Gramps's only creature and serves as a blocker behind Propaganda. With Sunblast Angel in hand (which destroys all tapped creatures), attacking with Baleful Strix taps it, making it vulnerable to effects and removing it as a blocker. More importantly, the 1 damage from Strix is negligible in a game where opponents are at 39 and 31 life. Keeping Strix back as a deathtouch blocker provides much more value than dealing 1 damage.

Only attacked with 1 creature instead of both. Zetalpa, Primal Dawn has vigilance (doesn't tap), is indestructible (can't be destroyed in combat), and deals 8 damage with double strike + flying. There's essentially zero risk to attacking with it, and leaving 8 damage on the table against a 31-life opponent is a meaningful mistake.

Declined to cast Prismatic Strands to prevent 4 damage from Zetalpa, Primal Dawn (an indestructible creature that will continue dealing damage each turn). The game offered it as a castable option during combat.

Failed to flash back Deep Analysis from the graveyard before casting Pristine Skywise. With River Kelpie on the battlefield, flashing back Deep Analysis would draw 3 cards (2 from Deep Analysis + 1 from River Kelpie's 'cast from graveyard' trigger) for just {1}{U} and 3 life. They had enough mana to cast both (9 mana available, 8 needed total). Casting card draw first provides more information before committing to a 6-mana creature.

GPT5m Gramps is attacking with Baleful Strix (1/1 flying deathtouch) into one of two remaining opponents. With Propaganda on the battlefield protecting them from attacks, their position is fairly defensive. Baleful Strix is a valuable defensive blocker with deathtouch that deters attackers. Attacking with it risks losing it to blocks (though flying helps) and removes it as a blocker. The 1 damage is minimal. More importantly, Gramps has Sunblast Angel in hand which destroys all tapped creatures - keeping Baleful Strix untapped would preserve it through a potential Sunblast Angel play on a future turn. However, since Sunblast Angel costs 6 mana and Gramps only has limited mana (Nimbus Maze, Swamp, Arcane Signet = roughly 3-4 mana available), this may not be immediately relevant. The attack is likely into Llama4 Valley or Kimi25 Libby - 1 flying damage is marginal but the risk of losing the deathtouch blocker is real.

Attacking with all creatures including Pristine Skywise risks losing the 6/4 flyer to Baleful Strix's deathtouch if attacking GPT5m Gramps, and River Kelpie is a valuable engine piece that could be kept back. Additionally, Propaganda taxes attacks against Gramps at 2 mana per creature.

Rootha, Mercurial Artist (1/4) could have blocked River Kelpie (3/3) and survived the combat, saving 3 damage at no cost. At 23 life facing multiple attackers including Zetalpa, preserving life total matters.

message: Select a permanent card with mana value 3 or less from your graveyard
annotation_description: With Sevinne's Reclamation on the stack, Llama4 Valley could have cast the Cooperate half of Refuse // Cooperate to copy Sevinne's Reclamation and return an additional permanent with mana value 3 or less from their graveyard to the battlefield (e.g., Guttersnipe, Commander's Sphere, or Burnished Hart). With River Kelpie on board, this would also trigger card draw. This is significant value left on the table.

Declined to cast Izzet Locket with mana available during postcombat main. With only 2 cards in hand (Farm // Market and Ignite the Future), deploying a mana rock would help cast Ignite the Future ({3}{R}) more efficiently and provide a future card draw option via its sacrifice ability.

Llama4 Valley has 7 lands in play (Mountain, Temple of the False God, Swiftwater Cliffs, Island, Plains, Island, Island) and Wind-Scarred Crag in hand but chose not to play it or cast any spells. They have several castable options: Deep Analysis flashback (1U + 3 life), Oona's Grace (2U), Sevinne's Reclamation (2W) to recur a permanent, or Ignite the Future (3R) to exile and potentially play cards. With only 3 cards in hand and River Kelpie on board (which draws cards when permanents enter from graveyard or spells are cast from graveyard), casting Deep Analysis flashback or Sevinne's Reclamation would generate card advantage through River Kelpie triggers. Additionally, they missed playing Wind-Scarred Crag as their land drop. With MiMo eliminated and only Kimi at 6 life, developing their board and generating card advantage is important.

Declined to cast Oona's Grace from graveyard via Retrace at end of turn, missing 2 card draws (1 from Grace, 1 from River Kelpie's trigger for casting from graveyard). Wind-Scarred Crag was a low-value discard, and mana was available and going to waste.

Kimi25 Libby cast Dualcaster Mage targeting Elemental Masterpiece on the stack. However, Elemental Masterpiece is a sorcery that creates two 4/4 Elemental tokens - copying it would give Kimi two additional 4/4 tokens, which is strong. But the issue is that the Elemental Masterpiece on the stack appears to be the discard ability of the card ('{U/R}{U/R}, Discard this card: Create a Treasure token'), not the sorcery itself being cast. Looking at the graveyard, Elemental Masterpiece is already in Kimi's graveyard, meaning it was discarded to create a Treasure token. Dualcaster Mage copies an instant or sorcery spell, but the Treasure-creating ability is an activated ability, not a spell. This means the Dualcaster Mage's ETB trigger would have no valid target and accomplish nothing beyond getting a 2/2 body. The Dualcaster Mage was wasted as a copy effect when it could have been held for a more impactful spell to copy later.

At end of turn with mana available (8 lands including Temple of the False God), Llama4 Valley declined to cast Oona's Grace from the graveyard using Retrace. With Wind-Scarred Crag in hand (a tapped land that could be discarded), they could pay 2U + discard Wind-Scarred Crag to draw a card via Retrace at instant speed. River Kelpie is on the battlefield and triggers when spells are cast from the graveyard, so casting Oona's Grace from the graveyard would also trigger River Kelpie to draw an additional card.
